t: The Independent State of Croatia was proclaimed in Zagreb on 10 April 1941 after the Axis invasion of Yugoslavia, and the Nuremberg Military Tribunal later concluded it was not a sovereign state.
The Ustaše regime killed an estimated 320,000–340,000 Serbs, 30,000 Croatian Jews and 30,000 Roma; Jasenovac was the largest of its 22 concentration camps.
Partisan resistance began in the NDH in June 1941, and the state ended in May 1945, its territory becoming part of Democratic Federal Yugoslavia.
dyk: The Duke of Aosta, named King Tomislav II of the state, never visited it; on learning of his nomination he thought it a bad joke by his cousin King Victor Emmanuel III.
ev: Slavko Kvaternik proclaims the Independent State of Croatia in Zagreb under German protection
Ante Pavelić returns from exile in Italy and takes power as Poglavnik
The Treaties of Rome cede central Dalmatia, most Adriatic islands and other lands to Italy
The Sisak Partisan Detachment, celebrated as the first armed resistance unit in occupied Yugoslavia, is formed
The first formal agreement between Bosnian Chetniks and the Ustaše authorities is concluded
After Italy's armistice the NDH declares the Treaties of Rome void and annexes the Dalmatian lands ceded to Italy
The Lorković-Vokić coup against Pavelić fails and its conspirators are executed
NDH forces and civilians retreat to Austria; the British hand them to the Partisans, and the state falls after the Battle of Odžak on 25 May

f.founder: Proclaimed by Slavko Kvaternik for Ante Pavelić, with German and Italian backing
f.predecessor: Kingdom of Yugoslavia (occupied by the Axis)
